news.title: Apple sharply cuts some employees’ daily AI budget
news.description: According to Bloomberg, Apple is reducing some engineers’ daily token budget from $300 to $200, with cuts of up to $25 for nontechnical teams. Employees may be directed to cheaper models or local AI.

news.title: ChatGPT can now generate GIFs from text or images
news.description: ChatGPT can turn text prompts or uploaded images into animated GIFs using Images 2.6. Users can adjust the speed, view images individually, and have a drawing completed before animation.

news.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Cyber, a model specialized in hacking
news.description: GPT-6 Cyber is a version of GPT-6 Astra designed to identify security vulnerabilities and write exploits. It scored 48.5% on ExploitGym, compared with 32.1% for GPT-5.6 Cyber, but access remains limited through Daybreak Red.

news.title: SpaceX opens Starfall missions to commercial customers
news.description: SpaceX has launched a commercial site for its Starfall reentry capsule, designed for microgravity experiments. Each mission can carry up to 1,000 kg, provide 1 kW and keep experiments connected via Starlink.

news.title: Markets plunge after the blue wave in the U.S. elections
news.description: The three major U.S. indexes fell sharply, with the Nasdaq dropping 5.52%. Data-center stocks, SpaceX and Tesla were hit particularly hard.

news.title: Google will disable its AI services for students by default
news.description: Google plans to disable its AI services for students by default next year, at schools’ request. The measure will include Google Search, which is considered an AI product.

news.title: Legal AI startup Harvey considers an IPO
news.description: Legal AI startup Harvey has held preliminary discussions about a possible IPO.

news.title: Snowflake’s former chief revenue officer joins an AI infrastructure startup
news.description: Snowflake’s former head of revenue is joining a little-known startup specializing in artificial intelligence infrastructure.

news.title: Three takeaways from Anthropic’s widely discussed AI report
news.description: The article presents three conclusions drawn from Anthropic’s report on artificial intelligence.

news.title: IREN blames Microsoft-requested network changes for delays to its AI project
news.description: IREN says network modifications requested by Microsoft are responsible for delays to its $9.7 billion artificial intelligence project.

news.title: Apple sharply cuts the waitlist for its new AI-powered Siri
news.description: Apple has substantially reduced the waitlist for access to its new artificial intelligence-powered version of Siri.

news.title: Aina opens preorders for a $399 smart ring
news.description: Aina has opened preorders for a ring equipped with a small screen, microphone, speaker and joystick. It can dictate notes, send queries to an agent, and control a Mac or phone; shipping is scheduled for January 2027.

news.title: Greg Brockman says OpenAI could be ready for an IPO in 2027
news.description: OpenAI President Greg Brockman said the company could be ready to go public in 2027. Its business revenue has roughly doubled and now represents the majority of its sales.

news.title: Airbnb is preparing an AI travel agent for the first half of 2027
news.description: Airbnb announced that its AI travel agent will arrive in the first half of 2027. It will build maps, comparisons, calendars and itineraries tailored to each request.

news.title: Meta makes its Muse agent capable of interruptible voice conversations
news.description: Meta’s Muse can now hold interruptible voice conversations, while an animated avatar reacts in real time. The feature is available on mobile, the web and Mac in the United States.

news.title: Baidu releases the files for its ERNIE 5.5 Flash base model
news.description: Baidu is providing researchers with the open files for a 280-billion-parameter model, with 14 billion parameters activated per token. ERNIE 5.5 Flash base has a one-million-token context window and can be fine-tuned.

news.title: Comedian Matt Husk, known for tricking ChatGPT, is being courted by labs
news.description: Followed by about two million people, Matt Husk films ChatGPT’s voice mode failing at simple tasks. OpenAI, Anthropic and xAI have offered to work with him, but he declined their offers.

news.title: Agility Robotics goes public with its Digit humanoid robot
news.description: Agility Robotics, the maker of the Digit robot, is going public through a SPAC despite substantial losses. Digit is already being used to move bins at several companies, and the future Digit 5 will be unveiled at CES 2027.

news.title: Australian universities want to train AI-native graduates
news.description: Several Australian universities are expanding access to ChatGPT and integrating AI into their courses. They want to prepare students for a labor market where collaborating with AI is becoming a core skill.

news.title: OpenAI admits it missed the coding-agent shift
news.description: Greg Brockman acknowledges that OpenAI was absent from the programming-assistant market, which is dominated by Claude Code. He says the enterprise business has since doubled and could prepare the company for an IPO as early as 2027.

news.title: Anthropic signs its first licensing deal with the Associated Press
news.description: Anthropic has reached an agreement with the Associated Press allowing Claude to display midterm election results with their sources. The decision marks a change in position after Anthropic invoked fair use to collect news content.

news.title: OpenAI drops confidentiality agreements with local officials
news.description: OpenAI will no longer sign NDAs with local officials hosting its data centers, except for security information or trade secrets. The agreements had been criticized for hiding negotiations from residents.

news.title: OpenAI expands its AI engineering tests from devices to vehicles
news.description: OpenAI used GPT-6 Astra to design a working prototype in less than a week, reducing initial design time. Tests conducted with Mazda and Chip Ganassi nevertheless show that manufacturing still requires human corrections.

news.title: The leading generative AI companies and startups to know
news.description: This guide presents the major and specialized players in generative AI, from OpenAI to niche providers. It covers uses including coding, creative media, healthcare and enterprise agents.

news.title: OpenAI pledges to fund the costs of its own data centers
news.description: OpenAI says it will cover all electricity and infrastructure costs for its data centers. Its commitment includes financial guarantees for utility customers and sharing data on water and electricity.

news.title: Demand for AI chips reduces the supply of Nintendo cartridges
news.description: Rising demand for AI memory chips is reducing the supply of ROM chips used in physical Nintendo Switch cartridges. Macronix, a Nintendo supplier, says its ROM production has fallen 39% year over year.

news.title: Sequoia reflects on two decades of expansion
news.description: Sequoia is narrowing its scope after two decades of expansion.

news.title: OpenAI to acquire Pierre Computer Company
news.description: OpenAI plans to acquire Pierre Computer Company, Inc.

news.title: Rare strike in Taiwan highlights tensions in the AI sector
news.description: A rare strike in Taiwan highlights the social tensions linked to the global rise of artificial intelligence.

news.title: Meta acquires AI coding startup Conductor
news.description: Meta is acquiring Conductor, a startup specializing in AI-assisted programming.

news.title: OpenAI showcases a 1.2 million dollar cybersecurity operation
news.description: OpenAI is highlighting a vulnerability-hunting workflow in which a single run costs 1.2 million dollars in tokens.

news.title: OpenAI speeds up physical product design with its models
news.description: OpenAI is sharing advances that allow its models to help engineers design, simulate and manufacture physical products. In an internal test, GPT-6 Astra defined the requirements and designed a device’s enclosure, circuit board and software integrations without direct human modifications.

news.title: Adobe brings its customer experience agents to major AI platforms
news.description: Adobe’s CX Enterprise Coworker is now available in ChatGPT, Claude, Databricks Genie, Gemini for business and Microsoft Copilot. These integrations allow marketers to access data and coordinate customer experience tasks across connected systems.

news.title: Google will invest 15 billion dollars in data centers in Malaysia
news.description: Google has announced a 15 billion dollar investment in Malaysia over the next two years to build data centers and other infrastructure to meet growing demand for artificial intelligence services.

news.title: ChatGPT reportedly accounts for about 20% of Google’s search volume
news.description: OpenAI Chief Product Officer Adam Fry says ChatGPT has reached about 20% of Google’s search volume. If accurate, the chatbot would be Google Search’s most serious challenger in decades.

news.title: Investors await jobs data after the tech plunge
news.description: U.S. stock futures were mixed on Friday ahead of the release of the October jobs report.

news.title: Goldman Sachs names 109 new partners, the most since 2010
news.description: Goldman Sachs welcomed 109 members into its partnership, its largest class since 2010. The number of engineers reached a record high amid Wall Street’s growing interest in AI.

news.title: Walleye fund fires its head of stock selection
news.description: After a difficult October, Walleye dismissed its head of equity selection, Anil Gondi, along with a significant share of its equity portfolio managers. The $17 billion fund lost nearly 6% last month.

news.title: Major investors debate AI and the future of the labor market
news.description: At the SALT London forum, financial figures discussed the rise of AI, the outlook for the job market and Elon Musk’s predictions.

news.title: Tesla will gradually halt Cybertruck production
news.description: Elon Musk announced that Tesla will gradually reduce Cybertruck production starting in the middle of next year. The space freed up at the Texas plant will be used to build the Cybercab robotaxi.

news.title: Mira Murati’s startup targets a $5 billion funding round
news.description: Thinking Machines Lab, Mira Murati’s AI startup, is seeking to raise $5 billion at a $40 billion pre-money valuation. Accel is leading the round, which could more than triple the company’s valuation.

news.title: Block announces another wave of layoffs
news.description: Jack Dorsey’s fintech is cutting jobs for the second time this year, despite reporting better-than-expected results just days earlier. Employees in the Cash App business are affected.

news.title: Disney employees demand answers from management
news.description: After several major rounds of layoffs this year and the prospect of another workforce reduction, Disney employees say morale is suffering. Some asked executives for answers at a recent town hall.

news.title: Nvidia must decide how to financially support neoclouds
news.description: Nvidia helped bring about a generation of cloud-service providers specializing in AI. The company must now determine how much support to provide as financing becomes more expensive.

news.title: Americans are choosing gift recipients more carefully
news.description: Americans are becoming more selective about whom they will give a gift to this year.

news.title: Cristiano Ronaldo will retire from international football at 41
news.description: Cristiano Ronaldo says he will retire from international football at the age of 41. The article also examines the scientific factors behind his longevity.

news.title: Loved ones pay tribute to Learjet crash victim Helen Sharp
news.description: Helen Sharp, who died at 40 in a Learjet crash, is described by friends as someone who lived life to the fullest.

news.title: Bryan Cranston describes his life between New York and Los Angeles
news.description: The actor and co-founder of the Dos Hombres mezcal brand explains how he divides his time between New York and Los Angeles.

news.title: Data-center builders speak out after the elections
news.description: Data-center builders gathered during the midterm elections and shared their views.

news.title: Amazon Prime adds a restaurant meal-delivery benefit
news.description: Amazon Prime members are receiving a new benefit related to restaurant meal delivery.

news.title: Student-loan repayment difficulties are worsening
news.description: Lawmakers say student-loan repayment problems are growing and are demanding answers.

news.title: Michael Burry criticizes Anthropic’s strategy and refuses to buy its stock
news.description: Michael Burry believes Anthropic is betting its entire existence on optimism and says he does not plan to buy its stock.

news.title: A carpenter becomes financially independent by renting out land
news.description: A carpenter who went bankrupt achieved financial independence through an unusual land-rental business.

news.title: AI infrastructure stocks drive the S&P 500 down 4.4%
news.description: AI infrastructure stocks triggered a Wall Street sell-off as investors anticipated a slowdown in data center construction. The S&P 500 fell 4.4%.

news.title: Claude rolls out a personal finance management hub
news.description: Claude’s Personal Finance hub is gradually rolling out to U.S. Pro, Max and Ultra subscribers. It connects to bank accounts and cards through Plaid to categorize spending, spot duplicates and explain fees, in read-only mode.

news.title: Gauge turns AI agent errors into regression tests
news.description: The open-source Gauge tool has coding agents perform the same task, records their sessions and checks the results against success or failure criteria. It lets users modify an instruction, rerun exactly the same task and compare the results.

news.title: Anthropic gives METR internal access to measure AI progress
news.description: Anthropic gave METR internal access, and the organization estimates that AI capabilities on well-specified tasks are advancing roughly twice as fast as a year ago.

news.title: A contest offers one million dollars for five materials science problems
news.description: Discovered Materials is offering one million dollars for five unresolved materials science problems. Leading AI agents have so far made little progress on them.

news.title: ElevenMusic publishes AI-generated tracks directly to SoundCloud
news.description: ElevenMusic now lets users publish AI-generated tracks directly to SoundCloud. Users have created more than 25 million tracks with ElevenLabs’ music models.

news.title: Box Context Retrieval answers questions from authorized files
news.description: Box Context Retrieval uses NVIDIA Nemotron models to answer only from files the user can access, including scanned documents, images, audio and video. General availability is planned for early 2027.

news.title: Axiom releases a 16-million-line Lean formalization of the Stacks Project
news.description: Axiom released a Lean formalization of the Stacks Project consisting of 16 million lines, produced primarily by swarms of AI agents. The agents also identified dozens of statements requiring correction in the original text.

news.title: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash generates 15-second videos at lower cost
news.description: Google DeepMind is making Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash available to everyone, with clips of up to 15 seconds priced at $0.07 per second in 720p. The model can also edit a video conversationally without regenerating the entire thing.

news.title: Claude analyzes bank statements and detects unusual spending
news.description: Anthropic is launching Personal Finance, a Claude hub connected to bank accounts and credit cards through Plaid. Available in beta in the United States to certain subscribers, it analyzes spending in read-only mode and identifies duplicate payments and unexpected fees, among other things.

news.title: AI could help establish a dialogue with dolphins
news.description: A team of biologists from Georgia Tech and Google DeepMind is analyzing 40 years of dolphin recordings to identify patterns. It is also testing an underwater computer that emits sounds associated with objects, but it remains unclear whether this represents genuine understanding.

news.title: Anthropic reportedly accelerated its R&D through internal AI use
news.description: METR estimates that Anthropic’s models have been progressing roughly twice as fast since October as they did previously. The Information attributes this acceleration to the company’s intensive use of AI in research.

news.title: AI agents remain below a 12% success rate on a real-world work test
news.description: SemiAnalysis’s GDPx benchmark evaluates agents on simulated knowledge-work tasks, from chip design to quantitative trading. No model exceeds a 12% success rate, although Claude Opus 5.5 slightly outperforms Gemini 4 Carbon.

news.title: Microsoft Research aims to formally verify code written by AI agents
news.description: The PDD Kit tool turns a developer’s intent into a formal specification, then verifies that the generated code satisfies it for all possible inputs. Tested with GitHub Next’s Chopin, it uncovered bugs in an online store written in Rust.

news.title: NVIDIA opens four Cosmos 3 models for simulating realistic worlds
news.description: NVIDIA is releasing four 16-billion-parameter Cosmos 3 world models under a license permitting commercial use. They generate driving scenes, camera and LiDAR data, and simulations for autonomous cars and robots.

news.title: Grimes will appear in an AI-generated film intended for cinemas
news.description: The singer is lending her likeness and voice to « Gods Don't Give Gifts », a science-fiction film produced by Fable and scheduled for theatrical release on December 4. The studio wants to test the commercial potential of AI-generated cinema.

news.title: Grok Bot can now make phone calls on your behalf
news.description: The AI agent can wait on hold, schedule appointments and negotiate bills on U.S. numbers. The user remains the “caller of record,” and is therefore legally responsible for calls made by the bot.

news.title: Perplexity launches Teammates, collaborative AI agents for work
news.description: Teammates agents can take on different roles, work in parallel and reuse projects, skills and memories in Perplexity. The service relies on Perplexity Computer to handle long-running work.

news.title: Mistral adds managed agents and applications to Studio
news.description: Mistral is enhancing Studio with managed agents, workflows, observability and agent evaluation. The platform runs on Mistral Large 4 and can be deployed in the cloud, on a private network or on the company’s servers.

news.title: Tencent launches Hy4, a model capable of controlling a computer
news.description: Hy4 understands images and can use software autonomously. Tencent ranks it as the second Chinese model behind Kimi K3.1 Pro, while acknowledging its limitations in advanced mathematics and complex image analysis.

news.title: Beijing blocks SoftBank’s acquisition of ABB’s robotics division
news.description: China vetoed SoftBank’s acquisition of ABB’s robotics division through its foreign investment review agency. The decision highlights the growing strategic importance of industrial robots.

news.title: U.S. elections threaten the expansion of AI data centers
news.description: Democrats now control the U.S. House and Senate, while data centers influenced several local elections. The AI industry expects more regulation and a slowdown in new infrastructure.

news.title: Blue Origin delays New Glenn’s return to flight until January 2027
news.description: Jeff Bezos’s rocket is awaiting the reconstruction of its Cape Canaveral launch pad, destroyed by an explosion in May. Amazon is meanwhile using United Launch Alliance and Arianespace to deploy its satellite constellation.

news.title: AI stocks plunge after the U.S. elections
news.description: The Nasdaq fell 5.5%, while several chipmakers dropped more than 9% or by double digits. Wall Street fears a slowdown in data centers after the adoption of numerous local measures aimed at restricting them.

news.title: The AI data center boom sparks a backlash after the U.S. elections
news.description: Voters challenged the growth of AI-focused data centers. New restrictions could slow construction, raise costs and change the distribution of AI capacity.

news.title: 16 or 32 GB of RAM: Which capacity should you choose for a Windows AI laptop?
news.description: 16 GB is still enough for browsing, office work and cloud-based AI, while Windows 11 updates improve the performance of computers with limited memory. The article details the use cases that genuinely justify 32 GB.

news.title: AI agent governance: Who manages access and accountability?
news.description: New recommendations indicate that 71% of organizations give agents sensitive access, but only 35% use identity and access management. They recommend appointing owners, logging decisions and testing shutdown mechanisms.

news.title: Apple and Google face pressure over more than 400 deepfake-related sites
news.description: More than 400 apps and sites linked to deepfakes designed to undress people evaded Apple and Google’s controls. Hidden remote servers and ad-triggered features bypassed checks, while takedowns may not dismantle the abusive network.

news.title: Xiaomi begins rolling out Android 17 HyperOS 4
news.description: HyperOS 4 will reach 82 Xiaomi, Redmi and Poco devices in three waves through December 2026. The update includes a new interface, Super XiaoAi 2.0 with AI features, and performance and HDR improvements for apps.

news.title: Goldman Sachs names 109 new partners, its largest class since 2010
news.description: The bank promoted 109 executives to partner, one of Wall Street’s most coveted titles. It is the largest class since 2010, and the full list is available.

news.title: Apple will scan public iCloud links for dangerous content
news.description: Apple will begin scanning images and files shared through public iCloud links in iOS 27.3 and related systems. The company may move or delete affected files, block the Apple account and contact authorities.

news.title: Pangram says its new models detect fake content
news.description: Pangram says its new models can identify AI-generated content in images and videos.

news.title: AI agents are almost nonexistent for booking an Uber
news.description: Uber says almost nobody uses AI agents to book rides.

news.title: Amazon replaces Grubhub with Uber Eats in its app
news.description: Amazon is dropping Grubhub and integrating Uber Eats into its own app.

news.title: Apple allows discounts to retain users who attempt to cancel
news.description: Apple now allows developers to offer discounts to users who try to cancel their subscriptions.

news.title: Waymo confirms a change in its relationship with Uber in 2028
news.description: Waymo confirms that its relationship with Uber will change in January 2028.

news.title: DuckDuckGo turns to schools after controversy over Google
news.description: DuckDuckGo is offering its services to schools amid criticism of Google’s AI policy.

news.title: Discord moves away from Electron in favor of Rust
news.description: Discord is gradually replacing Electron with Rust, with an initial Windows version using 290 MB of RAM.

news.title: Early access to AI helps detect more vulnerabilities
news.description: A group of U.S. technology companies with early access to vulnerability-research tools more than doubled their reported flaws and found about 150% more critical vulnerabilities before they were exploited.

news.title: AI agents design low-carbon power grid plans
news.description: Power-planning agents produced valid, low-cost plans in all forty test cases, using only public data and adhering to strict carbon-emissions limits.

news.title: Web agents fall for scams in 11% to 35% of tests
news.description: A testing method recreates real fraudulent websites to measure how well AI assistants resist scams during shopping or banking operations. The agents were deceived between 11% and 35% of the time.

news.title: Government content removals divide Americans
news.description: A Pew-Knight survey indicates that 51% of American adults support the government removing false information, but only 14% support it when the information is deemed politically biased.

news.title: VMware returns to small deployments with vSphere Express
news.description: Broadcom has introduced vSphere Express for deployments of up to 128 processor cores, offering an alternative to VMware’s larger offerings. The solution includes live virtual machine migration, automated recovery and distributed switching, but individual installations cannot be centrally managed.

news.title: CrowdStrike launches a kill switch for AI agents
news.description: CrowdStrike’s new AI Kill Switch allows security teams to block agents’ access to AI models through connected gateways. Broader controls, such as stopping endpoint processes and revoking permissions, are still in development.

news.title: Disaster recovery must evolve for AI-centric businesses
news.description: Growing reliance on AI as operational infrastructure and on external services requires disaster recovery strategies to be rethought. Experts recommend defining a minimum viable business that includes AI models, RAG data and identity dependencies, while accounting for nondeterministic results and fast-moving autonomous agents.

news.title: Siloed AI projects increase business costs
news.description: AI projects run separately by department create hidden costs from duplicate platform purchases, repeated data preparation and unmonitored model usage. A shared inventory of tools and pilot projects makes it possible to compare operating costs with measurable benefits.

news.title: Snowflake announces Business Ontology to provide AI with business context
news.description: Snowflake has announced the upcoming public preview of Business Ontology, a business modeling and governance layer in Snowflake Horizon Context. It allows concepts, metrics and relationships to be defined and linked to underlying semantic views so AI agents use approved enterprise definitions.

news.title: Mozilla AI launches Otari to govern AI usage
news.description: Mozilla AI has launched Otari, an open-source operating system and gateway for AI governance and choosing between multiple providers. The platform allows organizations to restrict tools, manage user budgets and track AI sessions from one place.

news.title: MongoDB brings real-time Atlas data to Microsoft 365 Copilot
news.description: MongoDB’s Atlas connector, now generally available, allows Microsoft 365 Copilot to answer questions using real-time operational data. The integration uses a managed MCP server to query Atlas directly for orders, incidents and business metrics.

news.title: Neo4j and Snowflake combine graphs and enterprise data for AI
news.description: Neo4j and Snowflake have partnered to integrate Neo4j’s graph intelligence capabilities into Snowflake AI Data Cloud. It offers Virtual Graph for querying data without moving it, Graph Analytics for Snowflake for on-demand SQL algorithms and AuraDB for mission-critical real-time workloads.

news.title: Microsoft details Windows management changes and upcoming deadlines
news.description: Microsoft’s latest IT recap presents Windows recovery improvements and Intune controls allowing standard users to change certain approved network settings. It also notes the expiration of Windows Update certificates in 2027 and the end, on January 15, of CNAME-based discovery for MDM-only enrollment.

news.title: Confluent introduces Streamhouse to provide real-time business context
news.description: Confluent’s Streamhouse architecture combines streaming, processing, governance and querying to give applications and AI agents a continuously updated view of business operations.

news.title: IBM launches a managed version of HashiCorp Vault on dedicated infrastructure
news.description: IBM Cloud Secrets Manager Vault Dedicated provides single-tenant Vault Enterprise deployments, with IBM managing the infrastructure and operations. The service includes dynamic credentials, automated rotation and policy-based access.

news.title: Varda manufactures drugs in microgravity
news.description: Varda Space Industries uses autonomous orbital factories to process materials in small laboratories before returning a capsule to Earth. The company plans seven missions in 2027 and ten in 2028.

news.title: X.com rebuilds its web app with five engineers and AI agents
news.description: X.com’s new web application was developed by five engineers working with AI coding agents in less than six months. It loads significantly faster than the old version on slow connections and already serves logged-out users.

news.title: Design engineers use prototypes to shape future software
news.description: Design engineers contribute to feature and architecture decisions in code while retaining their role as designers. Their position enables them to create compelling prototypes of future concepts.

news.title: Local opposition to data centers gains ground in the United States
news.description: Nearly all local measures put to a vote opposing data centers have passed or are on track to pass, except in North Dakota. This political constraint could keep AI in a state of scarcity longer than expected.

news.title: Voice remains underused as an interface for AI
news.description: Voice is presented as a natural interface, particularly for speaking freely with coding agents and capturing context. The article outlines several ways to use voice to interact with AI.

news.title: US AI capacity could reach a ceiling of 81 GW in 2027
news.description: US capacity dedicated to AI is expected to rise from 38 GW today to a ceiling of 81 GW in 2027.

news.title: Teams need to choose bugs to fix more carefully
news.description: It is no longer practical to fix every bug. Teams therefore need to be more selective about the problems they devote their efforts to.

news.title: YouTube is preparing Tamba, an experimental app with social features
news.description: Tamba could serve as a testing ground for social features rather than being a finished product.

news.title: The biggest AI spenders stagnate in the third quarter
news.description: AI adoption continues to grow among other companies, but spending by the top 1% of customers stagnated in the third quarter. Anthropic’s dollar growth also slowed.

news.title: Payments could replace advertising revenue in the agent era
news.description: Agents make advertising-based business models less effective. Agent-driven spending could offset part of the decline in revenue.

news.title: Goldman Sachs limits AI coding tools for its technical teams
news.description: Goldman Sachs has limited the use of AI-based coding tools among its technical teams, excluding most traders and bankers for security reasons.

news.title: Create an on-demand data analyst with Grok Bot
news.description: The tutorial explains how to create a Bot dedicated to analyzing business data, connect it to data sources, and provide the necessary business context. The Bot can then be shared with the team and used from Team Bots or Slack.

news.title: Personal agents threaten the subscription economy
news.description: Agents can cancel subscriptions, negotiate bills, and move money into higher-yielding accounts. They could save customers time and money while disrupting entire industries.

news.title: Anthropic warns of the risk of critical thinking disappearing
news.description: Anthropic’s Addy Osmani believes critical thinking could disappear as agents become constantly available. His article on protecting this ability has surpassed three million views.

news.title: A Chrome extension replaces YouTube’s clickbait thumbnails
news.description: The De-Slopping YouTube Chrome extension replaces thumbnails designed to attract clicks with an image taken from the video, providing a better indication of what viewers will watch.

news.title: Claude Code subagents use 99% fewer resources
news.description: An update reduces Claude Code subagents’ resource consumption by 99%. Anthropic also published a roundup of the product’s major updates in October.
